record.paper_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
record.original_question: How should the community build offline reinforcement learning benchmarks and datasets that better reflect real deployment conditions by including stochastic dynamics, nonstationarity, risky biases in the data, and multiagent settings, so that algorithms can be evaluated on the kinds of failures and shifts that matter in practice?

evidence.quote: Current benchmarks still have insufficient datasets with stochastic dynamics in the environment (except for the Atari suite), common in real-world settings (e.g., economics, healthcare, education, and so on) and essential to evaluate. Environments that are nonstationary (i.e., change over time) are also very common in the real world and still have limited coverage in current benchmarks, only being present in the real-world RL suite. Furthermore, datasets designed to have risky biases are also important. For instance, if your driving data never shows a car crash, an offline RL algorithm should still be able to learn how to avoid car crashes. Finally, we have not found any offline RL datasets for multiagent environments, which may arise in settings like robot team navigation, smart grid operation, and control of mobile sensor networks [76].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the offline reinforcement learning setting in which a learner is given a fixed dataset D = {(s_i, a_i, r_i, s'_i)} of transitions collected from one or more behavior policies interacting with a Markov decision process (MDP) M = (S, A, P, r, γ), and must output a policy π: S → Δ(A) that aims to maximize the expected discounted return E_π[Σ_{t≥0} γ^t r_t] without further interaction with the environment. Standard offline RL benchmarks typically use datasets generated from MDPs with (approximately) deterministic dynamics, stationary transition kernels P, behavior policies that broadly cover state–action space, and a single agent.

Design and formalize a principled benchmark suite (specification of environments, data-collection protocols, evaluation metrics, and statistical evaluation procedures) for offline RL that simultaneously addresses each of the following four desiderata, and demonstrate that meaningful algorithmic distinctions emerge on it:

1. Stochastic dynamics: the environments must include MDPs whose transition kernels P(·|s,a) are genuinely stochastic (high-entropy, heavy-tailed, or with rare high-impact transitions), beyond the Atari Arcade Learning Environment.

2. Nonstationarity: the environments must include processes whose transition or reward functions vary with time, i.e., P_t and r_t with explicit nontrivial drift or regime change, and offline datasets that span multiple regimes.

3. Risky biases in the data: the datasets must be constructed so that certain catastrophic or safety-critical events (e.g., terminal failure states with large negative reward) are absent or strongly under-represented in D, while the evaluation tests whether the learned policy avoids those events at deployment.

4. Multi-agent settings: the suite must include cooperative and/or competitive multi-agent MDPs (Markov games) with offline trajectory data collected from fixed joint behavior policies, and metrics that evaluate offline learning of decentralized or centralized policies.

Provide (a) precise mathematical definitions of each environment class and of the associated dataset-generation distributions, (b) evaluation metrics that quantify performance under distributional shift, robustness to nonstationarity, avoidance of under-represented risky outcomes, and multi-agent coordination quality, and (c) baseline theoretical or empirical results separating known offline RL algorithms on the proposed benchmark.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an open research-program-style problem about constructing offline RL benchmarks. While individual partial efforts exist (e.g., D4RL, RL Unplugged, real-world RL suite, NeoRL, off-policy multi-agent datasets), no unified benchmark suite simultaneously addressing stochastic dynamics, nonstationarity, risky data biases, and multi-agent settings has been established as standard, and the question is still treated as open in the offline RL literature.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Current benchmarks still have insufficient datasets with stochastic dynamics ... nonstationary ... risky biases ... we have not found any offline RL datasets for multiagent environments.
status_evidence.claim: The four benchmark desiderata are listed as outstanding gaps in offline RL evaluation.
